entries.title: Forgotten particle could answer mystery of why we exist, say physicists
entries.summary: Scientists have unveiled a new theory on the birth of the cosmos, suggesting the early universe was shaped by an ancient particle that has been overlooked for decades.

entries.title: Custom frame timing captures ultrafast events across five orders of magnitude in time
entries.summary: Most conventional methods of ultrafast photography use evenly spaced intervals in which images are taken, but new developments have shown how much can be left out of the story, especially when multiple timescales are involved.

entries.title: Steering electrons with extreme ultraviolet light—team achieves quantum coherent control
entries.summary: Light is one of the most powerful tools scientists have for probing matter. By interacting with electrons, light reveals how atoms, molecules and materials are structured and how they evolve in time. Highly energetic ultraviolet and X-ray photons are particularly attractive…

entries.title: Individual atomic collisions can now be detected in the lab, potentially opening up pathways to new physics
entries.summary: Tiny atoms and molecules are constantly bombarding each other all around us. While we regularly measure the large-scale effects of these interactions, measuring the effect of each individual collision is far more difficult. But now, researchers have managed to measure how tiny…

entries.title: Fibres and glasses are competing material states in protein condensation
entries.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03415-z Fibres are thought to emerge from a dense protein condensate ageing into a glassy state. It is now shown that protein fibres and glassy condensates may result from two competing ageing pathways.

entries.title: A liquid-crystal analogue of the skyrmion Hall effect
entries.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03379-0 Magnetic skyrmions are known to exhibit a Hall effect in the presence of an electric current. Now it is shown that liquid-crystal solitons also exhibit a Hall-like drift under shear flow.
